newsitem.title: CANADA: Gulf Canada agrees to acquire Stampeder.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Canada agrees to acquire Stampeder.

text.p: Gulf Canada Resources Ltd. said Monday it agreed to acquire Stampeder Exploration Ltd. in a friendly stock swap deal valued at about C$1 billion ($720 million).
Gulf, which last month was outbid by PanCanadian Petroleum Ltd. for CS Resources Ltd., said it would offer 0.69124 of a Gulf share for each Stampeder share.

The board of Calgary-based Stampeder agreed to pay Gulf a C$20 million ($14.4 million) breakup fee if the deal was unsuccessful under certain circumstances, including a successful competing bid for Stampeder.

Gulf Chief Executive J.P. Bryan said in a statement that Stampeder's heavy oil assets, employees and technology in Western Canada complement Gulf's and will allow Gulf to continue to expand its heavy oil operations."

Bryan added that "a significant portion of Stampeder's conventional assets complement Gulf's assets in the House Creek/Panny/Senex and Bigoray areas in Alberta. In addition, Stampeder has 1.8 million net undeveloped acres, which we have reviewed and view as highly prospective both from heavy oil and conventional oil and gas perspectives."
Gulf said the offer represented a 31 percent premium over Stampeder's closing stock price of C$5.70 ($4.10) on Friday.

The exchange ratio was based on the July 24 closing share price of C$10.85 ($7.81) for Gulf and a value of C$7.50 ($5.40) for each Stampeder share. It is based on 98.5 million shares outstanding on a fully diluted basis and about C$300 million ($216 million) in net debt.
Stampeder shares rose C$1.35 to C$7.05 in early trading on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Monday. Gulf was down C15 cents to C$10.65 in Toronto.
Stampeder Chief Executive Jeff Tonken said his company approached Gulf with the friendly transaction.
